questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. When normal or positive personal pronouns are combined, they follow the 2-3-1 rule (Second Person $\rightarrow$ Third Person $\rightarrow$ First Person). Here, You (2), he (3) and I (1) is perfectly ordered.

questions.question: The legal team instructed that (A) / everyone of the witnesses must register (B) / their biometrics before entering the courtroom. (C) / No Error (D)
options: everyone of the witnesses must register
their biometrics before entering the courtroom.
questions.explanation: "Everyone" is an indefinite singular pronoun, requiring singular tracking forms. Change "their biometrics" to "his or her biometrics".

questions.question: This is the most complex assignment (A) / which has ever been handed over (B) / to our research and development department. (C) / No Error (D)
options: This is the most complex assignment
which has ever been handed over
to our research and development department.
questions.explanation: When a relative clause modifies an antecedent preceded by a superlative degree adjective (the most complex), you must use the relative pronoun "that" instead of "which". Change "which" to "that".

questions.question: Let he and his brother (A) / take charge of the logistics management (B) / for the upcoming international summit. (C) / No Error (D)
options: take charge of the logistics management
questions.explanation: The verb "Let" must always be followed by pronouns in the objective case. Change "Let he and his brother" to "Let him and his brother".

questions.question: The stray dog wagged it's tail (A) / enthusiastically when the young child (B) / offered it a piece of fresh bread. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The stray dog wagged it's tail
offered it a piece of fresh bread.
questions.explanation: It's = Contraction of "It is" or "It has". Its = Possessive pronoun. The sentence requires a possessive modifier for the tail. Change "it's" to "its".

questions.question: Neither of the two candidates (A) / have brought their original documents (B) / for the document verification round. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: "Neither" means none of the two, which is singular. It requires both a singular verb and a singular pronoun. Change "have brought their" to "has brought his".

questions.question: The manager explicitly told the staff (A) / that it was him who had cleared (B) / the pending invoice files yesterday. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The manager explicitly told the staff
that it was him who had cleared
questions.explanation: Following a form of the verb to be ("was"), use the subjective pronoun form. Change "it was him" to "it was he".

questions.question: Such students who do not take (A) / regular mock tests seriously fail (B) / to perform well in the actual exam. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Such students who do not take
to perform well in the actual exam.
questions.explanation: The correlative demonstrative adjective phrase "Such" must be paired with the relative pronoun "as" rather than "who" when introducing a category example. Change "Such students who" to "Such students as".

questions.question: The stray cat scratched itself (A) / when it tried to jump over (B) / the sharp barbed wire fence. (C) / No Error (D)
options: when it tried to jump over
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The reflexive pronoun "itself" correctly matches the singular neuter-gendered animal subject "cat".

questions.question: I, you and he (A) / have committed a serious blunder (B) / during the accounting calculation process. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: When personal pronouns are combined to express a mistake, guilt, crime, or negative situation, the ordering rule flips from 2-3-1 to the 1-2-3 rule (First Person → Second Person → Third Person). Change the order to "I, you and he" (which is correct as written, meaning the question checks your validation of this rule). Let's re-verify the question prompt text: "I, you and he" is indeed 1-2-3, making this section correct.

questions.question: He is the same gentleman (A) / who met me at the banking terminal (B) / last Tuesday afternoon. (C) / No Error (D)
options: who met me at the banking terminal
questions.explanation: When an antecedent is modified by the phrase "the same", it must be followed by the relative pronoun "that", never "who" or "which". Change "who" to "that".

questions.question: The long-awaited vacation packages offered (A) / by the tourism agency are cheaper (B) / than our competitors. (C) / No Error (D)
options: by the tourism agency are cheaper
questions.explanation: This is a faulty comparison trap. You cannot compare packages directly to competitors. Change "than our competitors" to "than those of our competitors" (where "those" perfectly stands in for the plural packages).

questions.question: The multi-national firm is planning (A) / to shift their primary headquarters (B) / from London to Singapore next year. (C) / No Error (D)
options: from London to Singapore next year.
questions.explanation: "Firm" is a singular collective noun acting as a single cohesive unit here. It must take the singular possessive pronoun "its" rather than the plural "their". Change "their primary" to "its primary".

questions.question: The principal distribution of tasks (A) / was carried out between (B) / all the members of the administrative cell. (C) / No Error (D)
options: all the members of the administrative cell.
questions.explanation: "Between" is used for exactly two items. When dealing with more than two items, use the preposition "among". Change "between" to "among".

questions.question: Whomever is chosen by the selection (A) / panel will have to undergo (B) / a rigorous medical evaluation process. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Whomever is chosen by the selection
questions.explanation: The pronoun acts as the direct subject for the verb phrase "is chosen" inside the subject clause. It must be in the subjective pronoun case. Change "Whomever" to "Whoever".

questions.question: The internal technical audit revealed (A) / that the building's roof requires (B) / immediate structural reinforcement works. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: In standard grammar rules, an apostrophe-s ('s) possessive marker cannot be appended to non-living objects (building's roof). Instead, possession must be shown using the "of" structure. Change "the building's roof" to "the roof of the building".

questions.question: It is a scientifically proven fact (A) / that the copper is a highly efficient (B) / conductor of electrical current waves. (C) / No Error (D)
options: It is a scientifically proven fact
that the copper is a highly efficient
questions.explanation: Omission of Articles Rule: Do not place a definite article (the) before materials or substances (copper, iron, gold) when speaking about them in a general sense. Remove "the" before copper.

questions.question: The ongoing cross-border trade dispute (A) / has caused a great damage (B) / to the bilateral diplomatic relationship. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: "Damage" is an uncountable abstract noun. Placing the indefinite article "a" before it is a grammatical infraction. Change "a great damage" to "great damage".

questions.question: The commanding officer instructed his infantry (A) / to take a two-miles walk (B) / down the rugged mountain terrain. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The commanding officer instructed his infantry
questions.explanation: In a hyphenated or compound noun modifier construct (a two-mile walk), the modifying noun component acting as an adjective can never take a plural form. Change "a two-miles walk" to "a two-mile walk".

questions.question: He always carries a pack of (A) / cards in his travel bag to pass (B) / the time during long transit hours. (C) / No Error (D)
options: He always carries a pack of
cards in his travel bag to pass
the time during long transit hours.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The collective noun phrase "a pack of cards" is grammatically standard.

questions.question: My father's friend's son (A) / has cleared the civil services exam (B) / on his very first attempt this year. (C) / No Error (D)
options: has cleared the civil services exam
on his very first attempt this year.
questions.explanation: Double Possessive Rule: Avoid using consecutive apostrophe-s constructions (father's friend's). Rephrase the sentence using the "of" structure to break the chain. Change to: "The son of my father's friend".

questions.question: The dynamic marketing executive (A) / is an university graduate with (B) / a specialization in digital media metrics. (C) / No Error (D)
options: a specialization in digital media metrics.
questions.explanation: Choice of a vs. an depends on the initial phonetic sound, not the actual vowel letter. "University" begins with a consonant sound ("yoo"). Therefore, change "an university" to "a university".

questions.question: He told the investigation panel (A) / that he had forgotten his spectacle (B) / inside the corporate locker vault. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that he had forgotten his spectacle
questions.explanation: Certain items worn or handled as pairs (spectacles, scissors, trousers, binoculars) are always plural in form and require an 's' ending. Change "spectacle" to "spectacles".

questions.question: The financial advisory firm provided (A) / multiple valuable advices to the clients (B) / regarding equity investment options. (C) / No Error (D)
options: multiple valuable advices to the clients
questions.explanation: "Advice" is an uncountable noun and cannot be pluralized into "advices". To express a plural count, use countable counters. Change "multiple valuable advices" to "multiple pieces of valuable advice".

questions.question: The prime minister addressed (A) / the nation from the ramparts (B) / of the Red Fort last morning. (C) / No Error (D)
options: of the Red Fort last morning.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. Historic monuments (the Red Fort, the Taj Mahal) correctly require the definite article "the".

questions.question: All the physics apparatuses (A) / in the laboratory were found to be (B) / damaged during the sudden shifting process. (C) / No Error (D)
options: in the laboratory were found to be
damaged during the sudden shifting process.
questions.explanation: The plural form of the noun apparatus is either apparatus or apparatuses in generic contexts, but in standard regulatory scientific listings, apparatus itself serves as the plural collective, or pieces of apparatus is preferred to clean up formatting. Change to "pieces of physics apparatus".

questions.question: It is a well-known fact that (A) / a honest individual will never (B) / compromise on his core moral values. (C) / No Error (D)
options: It is a well-known fact that
compromise on his core moral values.
questions.explanation: The word "honest" begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel sound ("ah-nest"). It must be preceded by "an" instead of "a". Change to "an honest individual".

questions.question: The heavy machinery industry (A) / has entered a temporary slump (B) / due to a lack of raw materials. (C) / No Error (D)
options: due to a lack of raw materials.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. "Machinery" is correctly used as an uncountable mass noun.

questions.question: The cattle's pasture land (A) / was heavily waterlogged due to (B) / the continuous monsoon downpour. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: "Cattle" is a plural noun that does not end in 's'. To show possession for a plural noun that does not end in 's', add an apostrophe followed by 's' (cattle's). The grammar structure here is correct, but let's look closer at the phrasing: "The pasture land of the cattle" is the cleaner variant to avoid non-human possessive distortions. Change to "The pasture land of the cattle".

questions.question: He has been suffering from (A) / the measles for the past (B) / two consecutive weeks. (C) / No Error (D)
The manager rejected his application (A) / because he had not attached (B) / two passport-size photographs. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The phrase "passport-size photographs" is structurally flawless.

questions.question: The legislative assembly passed (A) / a bill granting additional funds (B) / to the old and the poor. (C) / No Error (D)
options: to the old and the poor.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. When a definite article is placed before an adjective (the old, the poor), it turns into a plural collective noun representing that entire group of people.

questions.question: He purchased three dozens bananas (A) / from the local fruit vendor (B) / to distribute among the children. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: When a definite numeral adjective (three, two, five) precedes words like dozen, hundred, thousand, million, these units must remain singular if followed immediately by a noun. Change "three dozens bananas" to "three dozen bananas".

questions.question: The information received from (A) / the border security outposts (B) / were highly alarming to the council. (C) / No Error (D)
options: were highly alarming to the council.
questions.explanation: "Information" is an uncountable noun and is strictly singular. It cannot take the plural verb "were". Change "were" to "was".

questions.question: The sun rises in east (A) / and sets in the west, (B) / maintaining a perfect celestial rhythm. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: Directions of the compass (the East, the West, the North) must always take the definite article "the". Change "in east" to "in the East".

questions.question: The local library house (A) / a vast collection of (B) / ancient poetries and manuscripts. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: "Poetry" is an uncountable collective noun and cannot be pluralized into "poetries". Change "poetries" to "poems" or "poetry".

questions.question: The sound of a explosion (A) / could be heard across (B) / a radius of five kilometers. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: "Explosion" begins with a vowel sound. It must be preceded by the indefinite article "an". Change "a explosion" to "an explosion".

questions.question: The commander-in-chiefs' conference (A) / was held at the defense ministry (B) / to review the border security grid. (C) / No Error (D)
options: was held at the defense ministry
to review the border security grid.
questions.explanation: For a compound noun (commander-in-chief), pluralization happens at the root word (commanders-in-chief), but possessive markers ('s) are appended to the very last word of the phrase. Change to "The commander-in-chief's conference".

questions.question: He has given me (A) / an five-hundred rupee note (B) / to purchase the required medication. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: The compound modifier phrase "five-hundred rupee" begins with a consonant sound ("f"). The indefinite article must switch to match it. Change "an five-hundred" to "a five-hundred".

questions.question: The principal reason for (A) / his academic failure is a lack (B) / of concentration and hard works. (C) / No Error (D)
options: his academic failure is a lack
questions.explanation: "Work" when meaning physical or mental effort is an uncountable noun and does not take a plural ending. Change "hard works" to "hard work".

questions.question: The sudden escalation of fuel prices (A) / has naturally resulted into a corresponding increase (B) / in the cost of essential daily commodities. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The sudden escalation of fuel prices
has naturally resulted into a corresponding increase
in the cost of essential daily commodities.
questions.explanation: The verb "result" takes the fixed preposition "in" when indicating an outcome, not "into". Change "resulted into" to "resulted in".

questions.question: Despite of the technical team working (A) / around the clock, the server breakdown issues (B) / could not be resolved before the market opened. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Despite of the technical team working
around the clock, the server breakdown issues
could not be resolved before the market opened.
questions.explanation: The preposition "Despite" is never followed by "of". It is equivalent to "In spite of". Change "Despite of" to "Despite" or "In spite of".

questions.question: The managing director emphasized on (A) / the absolute necessity of maintaining cross-departmental (B) / transparency during the restructuring phase. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the absolute necessity of maintaining cross-departmental
questions.explanation: When used as a active verb, "emphasize" takes a direct object without any preposition. Remove the superfluous preposition "on". (Note: The noun form does take a preposition, e.g., "lay emphasis on").

questions.question: The senior architect was highly proficient (A) / with designing eco-friendly residential spaces (B) / using sustainable bamboo composites. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The senior architect was highly proficient
questions.explanation: The adjective "proficient" requires the fixed preposition "in" when referring to an activity or field. Change "proficient with designing" to "proficient in designing".

questions.question: The internal investigation cell (A) / has accused the senior accountant for (B) / embezzling funds from the employee welfare reserve. (C) / No Error (D)
options: has accused the senior accountant for
embezzling funds from the employee welfare reserve.
questions.explanation: The verb phrase structure is "accuse someone of something", not "for". Change "accused the senior accountant for" to "accused the senior accountant of".

questions.question: After a prolonged discussion lasting (A) / for nearly four hours, the committee finally (B) / agreed with the terms proposed by the union leader. (C) / No Error (D)
options: for nearly four hours, the committee finally
agreed with the terms proposed by the union leader.
questions.explanation: Agree to a proposal, plan, or terms. Agree with a person. Since the object is "the terms", change "agreed with" to "agreed to".

questions.question: The security guards successfully prevented (A) / the unauthorized media personnel to enter (B) / the restricted zones of the aerospace facility. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the unauthorized media personnel to enter
the restricted zones of the aerospace facility.
questions.explanation: The verb "prevent" tracks with the preposition "from" followed by a gerund ($V_4$), rather than an infinitive ($to + V_1$). Change "prevented... to enter" to "prevented... from entering".

questions.question: The software update was completely (A) / incompatible to the older operating system (B) / installed on our office workstations. (C) / No Error (D)
options: incompatible to the older operating system
questions.explanation: "Incompatible" takes the fixed preposition "with", not "to". Change "incompatible to" to "incompatible with".

questions.question: During the annual general meeting, (A) / the junior operations analyst was called out (B) / to explain the sudden drop in quarterly revenue. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the junior operations analyst was called out
to explain the sudden drop in quarterly revenue.
questions.explanation: This is a phrasal verb contextual error. Call out means to shout or challenge someone publicly. Call upon or Call on means to formally invite or ask someone to speak or perform a duty. Change "called out" to "called upon" (or "called on").

questions.question: The brave soldiers patterns of bravery (A) / were highly conducive for generating a sense (B) / of intense patriotism among the youth. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The brave soldiers patterns of bravery
were highly conducive for generating a sense
of intense patriotism among the youth.
questions.explanation: The adjective "conducive" is always paired with the fixed preposition "to", not "for". Change "conducive for" to "conducive to".

questions.question: The sudden heavy downpour coped up with (A) / the infrastructure challenges, exposing the municipal (B) / corporation's total lack of urban flood preparedness. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The sudden heavy downpour coped up with
the infrastructure challenges, exposing the municipal
corporation's total lack of urban flood preparedness.
questions.explanation: The expression "cope up with" is a highly frequent colloquial error. The correct English phrasal verb meaning to manage or face a situation successfully is "cope with". Remove the superfluous "up".

questions.question: The local administration has been (A) / vestibulating relief material since (B) / the past three consecutive weeks. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: Use "for" to denote a duration or period of time ("the past three weeks"). "Since" is reserved strictly for a specific starting point in time (e.g., "since Monday"). Change "since" to "for".

questions.question: The multi-billion dollar conglomerate (A) / actively abstains from investing into high-risk (B) / cryptocurrency and unregulated digital derivative markets. (C) / No Error (D)
options: actively abstains from investing into high-risk
cryptocurrency and unregulated digital derivative markets.
questions.explanation: The phrasal combination "abstain from" correctly targets an action, but when referencing fields or directions after it, "investing" takes "in" rather than "into". Change "investing into" to "investing in".

questions.question: The young sub-inspector was accompanied with (A) / a heavily armed police contingent to raid (B) / the suspected illegal warehouses near the port. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The young sub-inspector was accompanied with
a heavily armed police contingent to raid
the suspected illegal warehouses near the port.
questions.explanation: When an animate entity or group accompanies a person in the passive voice, use "accompanied by". (Note: "Accompanied with" is used for inanimate attachments, like a fever accompanied with a rash). Change "accompanied with" to "accompanied by".

questions.question: The project team worked late into the night (A) / to ensure that the execution framework (B) / was in accordance to the client's guidelines. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The project team worked late into the night
to ensure that the execution framework
was in accordance to the client's guidelines.
questions.explanation: The standard idiomatic phrase is "in accordance with", not "in accordance to". Change "in accordance to" to "in accordance with".

questions.question: The research scholar was deeply absorbed with (A) / analyzing the medieval carbon dating samples (B) / inside the climate-controlled laboratory vault. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The research scholar was deeply absorbed with
analyzing the medieval carbon dating samples
questions.explanation: The adjective "absorbed" takes the preposition "in" when it means fully engaged or deeply interested in something. Change "absorbed with" to "absorbed in".

questions.question: Our sales division needs to coordinate (A) / closely with the logistics cell to look into (B) / the reasons behind the delayed export deliveries. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Our sales division needs to coordinate
closely with the logistics cell to look into
the reasons behind the delayed export deliveries.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The phrasal verb "look into" correctly means to investigate.

questions.question: The legal counsel advised the family (A) / not to comply to the aggressive out-of-court (B) / demands made by the opposition party. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The legal counsel advised the family
not to comply to the aggressive out-of-court
demands made by the opposition party.
questions.explanation: The verb "comply" must be paired with the fixed preposition "with", never "to". Change "comply to" to "comply with".

questions.question: The senior diplomat politely differed from (A) / his European counterpart on the specific clauses (B) / relating to cross-border carbon tax exemptions. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The senior diplomat politely differed from
his European counterpart on the specific clauses
relating to cross-border carbon tax exemptions.
questions.explanation: Differ from means to be dissimilar in traits/appearance. Differ with means to disagree in opinion. Because the context is an opinion clash on specific contract clauses, change "differed from" to "differed with".

questions.question: The technical committee consists of (A) / ten highly experienced software engineers (B) / drawn from various premier technology institutions. (C) / No Error (D)
options: drawn from various premier technology institutions.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. Note that "consist of" is equivalent to "comprise". (TCS frequently tricks students by using "comprise of", which is wrong, but "consist of" is completely correct).

questions.question: The state government has provided (A) / an administrative guarantee to compensate the farmers (B) / for any loss arising out of the sudden drought. (C) / No Error (D)
options: an administrative guarantee to compensate the farmers
for any loss arising out of the sudden drought.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The phrasal combo "arising out of" means originating from and is perfectly idiomatic.

questions.question: The young athlete was completely blind in (A) / his left eye due to a severe injury (B) / sustained during a training session in childhood. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The young athlete was completely blind in
his left eye due to a severe injury
sustained during a training session in childhood.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. Blind in an eye is used for literal loss of sight. Blind to is used metaphorically for faults (e.g., "blind to his son's mistakes").

questions.question: The continuous noise from the nearby (A) / construction site made it extremely difficult (B) / to concentrate on our academic revisions. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The continuous noise from the nearby
construction site made it extremely difficult
to concentrate on our academic revisions.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The verb "concentrate" correctly takes the preposition "on".

questions.question: The corporate vigilance team is currently (A) / inquiring for the suspicious financial transactions (B) / routed through offshore shell accounts. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The corporate vigilance team is currently
inquiring for the suspicious financial transactions
questions.explanation: Inquire into a matter means to investigate it. Inquire after someone's health means to ask how they are. Inquire of someone means to ask them a question. Change "inquiring for" to "inquiring into".

questions.question: The newly appointed operational manager (A) / is highly passionate about his work and (B) / prides himself for his punctual execution track record. (C) / No Error (D)
options: is highly passionate about his work and
prides himself for his punctual execution track record.
questions.explanation: The reflexive verb construction "pride oneself" requires the fixed preposition "on", not "for". (Note: The adjective form takes "proud of", but the verb form takes "pride oneself on"). Change "prides himself for" to "prides himself on".

questions.question: Scarcely had the international flight landed (A) / at the terminal runway than the ground security crew (B) / cordoned off the entire arrival zone. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Scarcely had the international flight landed
at the terminal runway than the ground security crew
cordoned off the entire arrival zone.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbial conjunctions like "Scarcely" and "Hardly" must always be paired with "when" or "before", never "than". "Than" is exclusively reserved for "No sooner". Change "than" to "when".

questions.question: Not only did the malicious malware encrypt (A) / the core corporate database files but it also demanded (B) / a massive ransom payment in cryptocurrency tokens. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Not only did the malicious malware encrypt
the core corporate database files but it also demanded
a massive ransom payment in cryptocurrency tokens.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The correlative pair "Not only... but also" is correctly utilized, and the inversion rule (Not only did the malware encrypt) is perfectly maintained.

questions.question: No sooner did the factory siren sound (A) / when the workers dropped their heavy tools (B) / and rushed out toward the main exit gate. (C) / No Error (D)
options: No sooner did the factory siren sound
when the workers dropped their heavy tools
and rushed out toward the main exit gate.
questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction phrase "No sooner" must always be followed by its fixed coordinate twin "than", never "when". Change "when" to "than".

questions.question: Both the operations manager (A) / as well as the head of quality assurance (B) / were summoned to present the compliance report. (C) / No Error (D)
options: as well as the head of quality assurance
were summoned to present the compliance report.
questions.explanation: The conjunction "Both" must be paired strictly with "and". Using "as well as" alongside "Both" creates a redundant and grammatically invalid coupling. Change "as well as" to "and".

questions.question: The project coordinator was highly confused (A) / whether to allocate the additional funds to marketing (B) / or to spend it entirely on technical research. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The project coordinator was highly confused
whether to allocate the additional funds to marketing
or to spend it entirely on technical research.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The alternative marker "whether" is correctly completed by its matching tracking partner "or".

questions.question: Unless you do not submit your original (A) / medical certificates to the administrative office, (B) / your medical leave extension will not be sanctioned. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Unless you do not submit your original
medical certificates to the administrative office,
your medical leave extension will not be sanctioned.
questions.explanation: The conditional conjunction "Unless" is inherently negative (meaning if not). Placing another negative term like "do not" inside the clause introduces an invalid double negative error. Change "Unless you do not submit" to "Unless you submit".

questions.question: Walk carefully lest you should not trip (A) / over the loose construction cables laid down (B) / across the main entrance hallway corridors. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Walk carefully lest you should not trip
over the loose construction cables laid down
across the main entrance hallway corridors.
questions.explanation: The adverbial conjunction "Lest" inherently carries a negative meaning (meaning for fear that). It is paired exclusively with the modal auxiliary verb "should", and no negative word like "not" or "never" can be placed inside its clause. Remove "not".

questions.question: Although the public sector bank faced (A) / massive bad loan write-offs this fiscal year, (B) / but it managed to declare a minor net profit margin. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Although the public sector bank faced
massive bad loan write-offs this fiscal year,
but it managed to declare a minor net profit margin.
questions.explanation: The concession conjunctions "Although" or "Even though" can be followed either by a comma or by the word "yet". They can never be coupled with the coordinating conjunction "but". Remove "but".

questions.question: The reason why he was rejected (A) / from the final campus placement rounds (B) / was because his communication skills were inadequate. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The reason why he was rejected
from the final campus placement rounds
was because his communication skills were inadequate.
questions.explanation: The phrase "The reason why" structurally denotes a cause. Pairing it with the conjunction "because" creates redundancy. Replace "because" with "that".

questions.question: He had no other choice (A) / but to tender his formal resignation (B) / after the corporate governance scandal broke out. (C) / No Error (D)
options: but to tender his formal resignation
after the corporate governance scandal broke out.
questions.explanation: The comparative adjectives "other" and "rather" must be followed by the conjunction "than" instead of "but". Change "but to tender" to "than to tender".

questions.question: The local defense unit had (A) / hardly completed the tactical trench fortifications (B) / than the enemy launched a surprise artillery strike. (C) / No Error (D)
options: hardly completed the tactical trench fortifications
than the enemy launched a surprise artillery strike.
questions.explanation: As established earlier, "Hardly" requires "when" or "before" to link its dependent clause, never "than". Change "than" to "when".

questions.question: Such was his brilliant performance (A) / that the entire auditorium stood up (B) / to give him a roaring standing ovation. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that the entire auditorium stood up
to give him a roaring standing ovation.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The combination "Such... that" is correctly applied to showcase cause and effect.

questions.question: The real estate company not only provides (A) / premium housing flats at highly affordable rates (B) / but also customized interior design setups. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The real estate company not only provides
premium housing flats at highly affordable rates
but also customized interior design setups.
questions.explanation: This is a conjunction parallelism trap. The elements following not only and but also must belong to identical parts of speech. But also is followed by a noun phrase ("customized interior design setups"). Not only is followed by a verb ("provides"). To balance the structure, shift the position of the verb. Change part A to: "The real estate company provides not only".

questions.question: Until the central government does not (A) / ease the direct tax compliance parameters, (B) / small-scale industrial units will struggle to survive. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Until the central government does not
ease the direct tax compliance parameters,
small-scale industrial units will struggle to survive.
questions.explanation: Similar to "unless", "Until" is a time-based negative conditional marker. It cannot tolerate a secondary "does not" inside its immediate clause. Change "Until the central government does not ease" to "Until the central government eases".

questions.question: No sooner had the prime minister finished (A) / his Independence Day speech then the massive crowd (B) / began dispersing from the historic grounds. (C) / No Error (D)
options: No sooner had the prime minister finished
his Independence Day speech then the massive crowd
began dispersing from the historic grounds.
questions.explanation: TCS frequently exploits the homophone trap between "than" (conjunction of comparison) and "then" (adverb of time). "No sooner" strictly requires the conjunction "than". Change "then" to "than".

questions.question: He is as intelligent, (A) / if not more intelligent than, (B) / his elder brother who works at NASA. (C) / No Error (D)
options: his elder brother who works at NASA.
questions.explanation: This is an incomplete comparison pairing trap. The positive degree structure requires the full correlative frame "as... as". Change "as intelligent" to "as intelligent as".

questions.question: Keep your configuration documentations ready (A) / so that the systems migration process can be (B) / executed without any unexpected technical glitch. (C) / No Error (D)
options: so that the systems migration process can be
executed without any unexpected technical glitch.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The compound conjunction "so that" correctly introduces a clause of purpose.

questions.question: The seasoned politician spoke in such a manner (A) / as everyone present in the press room (B) / believed his fabricated narratives blindly. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The seasoned politician spoke in such a manner
as everyone present in the press room
questions.explanation: When showing a result or consequence of a manner, use the combination "such a manner that" instead of "as". Change "as everyone" to "that everyone".

questions.question: He ran as fastly as he could (A) / but he still failed to catch (B) / the departing commuter express train. (C) / No Error (D)
options: He ran as fastly as he could
but he still failed to catch
questions.explanation: The word "fastly" does not exist in standard English vocabulary; "fast" functions as both an adjective and an adverb. Change "as fastly as" to "as fast as".

questions.question: Work systematically down the checklist (A) / lest you should miss out any critical parameters (B) / during the final safety validation inspection. (C) / No Error (D)
options: lest you should miss out any critical parameters
during the final safety validation inspection.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. "Lest" is correctly paired with the modal verb "should" without any negative terms nearby.

questions.question: The newly launched premium smartphone (A) / is neither sleek in its design (B) / or affordable for the middle-class segment. (C) / No Error (D)
options: is neither sleek in its design
or affordable for the middle-class segment.
questions.explanation: The negative correlative conjunction "neither" must be completed by "nor", never "or". Change "or affordable" to "nor affordable".

questions.question: The multi-national enterprise has announced (A) / that it will either scale up its manufacturing units (B) / otherwise downsize its non-performing staff. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that it will either scale up its manufacturing units
questions.explanation: The alternative conjunction "either" must be strictly paired with its partner "or". Using "otherwise" breaks this structure. Change "otherwise downsize" to "or downsize".

questions.question: No sooner the heavy metal gates opened (A) / than the eager enthusiasts flooded inside (B) / to grab the front-row event seats. (C) / No Error (D)
options: No sooner the heavy metal gates opened
than the eager enthusiasts flooded inside
to grab the front-row event seats.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with a negative adverbial phrase like "No sooner," the rule of grammatical inversion must be applied (the auxiliary verb must sit before the subject). Change "No sooner the heavy metal gates opened" to "No sooner did the heavy metal gates open" or "No sooner had the heavy metal gates opened".

questions.question: He did not question the validation (A) / of the technical parameters because of he trusted (B) / the core competency of the senior research head. (C) / No Error (D)
options: He did not question the validation
of the technical parameters because of he trusted
the core competency of the senior research head.
questions.explanation: "Because of" is a prepositional phrase and must be followed by a noun or pronoun. Since it is followed here by a full active clause (he trusted the core competency...), you must use the subordinating conjunction "because". Remove the word "of".

questions.question: Provided that you strictly adhere (A) / to the specified sterilization guidelines, (B) / the laboratory cultures will grow without contamination. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the laboratory cultures will grow without contamination.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The conditional conjunction phrase "Provided that" is used correctly to mean on the condition that.

questions.question: The research scientist discovered (A) / that the newly isolated bacterial strain (B) / is highly resistant to standard penicillin doses. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that the newly isolated bacterial strain
is highly resistant to standard penicillin doses.
questions.explanation: This is a trap involving the sequence of tenses. While a past-tense reporting verb (discovered) normally shifts the subordinate clause to the past tense, universal truths, scientific facts, and permanent realities remain strictly in the simple present tense. The resistance of the strain is a scientific fact, making "is" completely correct.

questions.question: If the finance ministry would have revised (A) / the direct tax slabs earlier, the domestic markets (B) / would have witnessed a much stronger recovery phase. (C) / No Error (D)
options: If the finance ministry would have revised
the direct tax slabs earlier, the domestic markets
would have witnessed a much stronger recovery phase.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional Rule: In a past conditional sentence showing an unfulfilled past action, the conditional clause (if-clause) must take the Past Perfect Tense (had + V_3), while the main clause takes would + have + V_3. You can never use "would have" in the if-clause. Change "would have revised" to "had revised".

questions.question: The administrative staff is maintaining (A) / these critical digital ledger records (B) / since the inception of the corporate cell. (C) / No Error (D)
options: since the inception of the corporate cell.
questions.explanation: When an action begins in the past and continues into the present—indicated by time markers like since or for—you must use the Present Perfect Continuous Tense instead of the Present Continuous. Change "is maintaining" to "has been maintaining".

questions.question: By the time the fire brigade personnel (A) / arrived at the suburban industrial estate, (B) / the fire completely destroyed two massive warehouses. (C) / No Error (D)
options: By the time the fire brigade personnel
arrived at the suburban industrial estate,
the fire completely destroyed two massive warehouses.
questions.explanation: When two connected actions occurred in the past, the older action (the first event) must be expressed in the Past Perfect Tense ($had + V_3$), while the subsequent action takes the Simple Past. The destruction of the warehouses happened before the brigade arrived. Change "completely destroyed" to "had completely destroyed".

questions.question: He told me that he was working (A) / in the software firm for five long years (B) / before he finally decided to pursue an MBA. (C) / No Error (D)
options: He told me that he was working
in the software firm for five long years
before he finally decided to pursue an MBA.
questions.explanation: Because the action was ongoing over a specific duration (for five long years) before another past anchor point (decided), it requires the Past Perfect Continuous Tense rather than the Past Continuous. Change "was working" to "had been working".

questions.question: The senior operations executive (A) / is working at our manufacturing facility (B) / for the past seven months now. (C) / No Error (D)
options: is working at our manufacturing facility
for the past seven months now.
questions.explanation: The presence of the duration marker "for the past seven months" flags an action anchored in the past stretching to the present. Change "is working" to the Present Perfect Continuous form: "has been working".

questions.question: When I will visit my native village (A) / next month, I will definitely distribute (B) / winter blankets to the local manual laborers. (C) / No Error (D)
options: When I will visit my native village
next month, I will definitely distribute
winter blankets to the local manual laborers.
questions.explanation: Future Conditional Constraint: In a sentence containing a future time clause or conditional clause introduced by markers like when, if, until, as soon as, you cannot use the auxiliary verb "will" or "shall" within that time clause. It must remain in the Simple Present. Change "When I will visit" to "When I visit".

questions.question: I have seen him yesterday (A) / at the crossroad traffic junction but he (B) / did not notice my vehicle passing by. (C) / No Error (D)
options: at the crossroad traffic junction but he
did not notice my vehicle passing by.
questions.explanation: If a sentence contains a specific past time marker (yesterday, last week, in 1947, two days ago), you must use the Simple Past Tense, never the Present Perfect. Change "I have seen him yesterday" to "I saw him yesterday".

questions.question: My younger sister is going (A) / to the state swimming academy (B) / every morning at six o'clock. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: Habitual Actions Rule: Regular habits, repeated routines, or permanent characteristics must always be framed in the Simple Present Tense, not the continuous tense. Change "is going" to "goes".

questions.question: It is high time the central environmental board (A) / takes strict punitive measures against (B) / the chemical factories polluting the river basin. (C) / No Error (D)
options: It is high time the central environmental board
the chemical factories polluting the river basin.
questions.explanation: Phrases like "It is high time," "It is time," or "It is about time" indicate a hypothetical scenario that should have already happened. They must be followed by a subject and a verb in the Simple Past Tense ($V_2$). Change "takes" to "took".

questions.question: The historical monument stands (A) / proudly at the city center (B) / for more than three centuries. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: The duration marker "for more than three centuries" forces the timeline out of the simple present state into a perfect aspect. Change "stands" to the Present Perfect state: "has stood".

questions.question: By next December, the technical core team (A) / will complete the software integration phase (B) / across all the global servers. (C) / No Error (D)
options: By next December, the technical core team
will complete the software integration phase
questions.explanation: When an action is expected to be finished by a specific future boundary limit denoted by "By + Future Time Word" (By next December), you must use the Future Perfect Tense ($will + have + V_3$). Change "will complete" to "will have completed".

questions.question: As soon as the regulatory panel will clear (A) / the safety compliance report, our company (B) / will commence the commercial production of vaccines. (C) / No Error (D)
options: As soon as the regulatory panel will clear
the safety compliance report, our company
will commence the commercial production of vaccines.
questions.explanation: The subordinating time conjunction "As soon as" introduces a time clause. As with Q207, avoid using "will" inside the time clause. Change "will clear" to the simple present form "clears".

questions.question: The senior management officer had left (A) / the office premises before the audit team (B) / had arrived to verify the transaction files. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The senior management officer had left
the office premises before the audit team
had arrived to verify the transaction files.
questions.explanation: This sentence misapplies the past perfect tense by doubling it. The older action ("had left") is correctly past perfect, so the subsequent action ("arrived") must be in the Simple Past Tense. Change "had arrived" to "arrived".

questions.question: The young child has been crying (A) / continuously for the past one hour (B) / because he had lost his favorite toy. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The young child has been crying
continuously for the past one hour
because he had lost his favorite toy.
questions.explanation: The main action ("has been crying") anchors the sentence's baseline context firmly in the present timeline. Therefore, a cause extending right up to this moment should be framed in the Present Perfect, not the past perfect. Change "had lost" to "has lost".

questions.question: I am knowing the primary suspect (A) / for several years, and I can confidently state (B) / that he is incapable of committing this crime. (C) / No Error (D)
options: I am knowing the primary suspect
for several years, and I can confidently state
that he is incapable of committing this crime.
questions.explanation: This sentence hits two traps. First, "know" is a stative verb (a verb of mental state) and cannot be used in a continuous form (am knowing). Second, the phrase "for several years" requires a perfect aspect. Change "I am knowing" to the Present Perfect form: "I have known".

questions.question: If I was you, I would immediately (A) / accept the lucrative international posting (B) / offered by the executive recruitment panel. (C) / No Error (D)
options: If I was you, I would immediately
offered by the executive recruitment panel.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional / Hypothetical Trap: When framing an imaginary, impossible, or purely hypothetical conditional statement (If I were you), the past subjunctive verb "were" must be used for all subjects, regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural. Change "If I was" to "If I were".

questions.question: The local defense unit successfully repulsed (A) / the enemy incursions because they received (B) / timely intelligence warnings from the command center. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The local defense unit successfully repulsed
the enemy incursions because they received
timely intelligence warnings from the command center.
questions.explanation: The receipt of the intelligence warnings happened prior to the successful defense action. To clearly sequence these past events, change the cause ("received") to the Past Perfect form: "had received".

questions.question: He behaves as if he knows (A) / everything about the secret diplomatic (B) / negotiations taking place behind closed doors. (C) / No Error (D)
options: He behaves as if he knows
negotiations taking place behind closed doors.
questions.explanation: The phrase "as if" or "as though" introduces an unreal, hypothetical condition. It must be followed by a verb in the Past Subjunctive / Simple Past form ($V_2$) to reflect this unreality. Change "knows" to "knew".

questions.question: My father did not yet receive (A) / the formal retirement pension orders (B) / from the central administrative cell. (C) / No Error (D)
options: My father did not yet receive
questions.explanation: The presence of the time adverb "yet" indicates that an action has not occurred up to the present moment. This requires the Present Perfect Tense alongside a negative marker, not the simple past. Change "did not yet receive" to "has not yet received".

questions.question: Unless the civic authorities will take (A) / prompt remedial actions, the city's drainage grid (B) / will collapse completely during the monsoon. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Unless the civic authorities will take
prompt remedial actions, the city's drainage grid
will collapse completely during the monsoon.
questions.explanation: Similar to standard time clauses, conditional clauses introduced by "Unless" or "Until" cannot contain the future auxiliary "will". Change "will take" to "takes".

questions.question: The laboratory technician told the director (A) / that the culture sample grew (B) / significantly overnight. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The laboratory technician told the director
questions.explanation: In indirect speech, if the reporting verb is in the past tense ("told"), actions that occurred prior to the reporting moment must shift backward on the timeline. Change "grew" to the Past Perfect form: "had grown".

questions.question: For over a decade now, (A) / our non-governmental organization is working (B) / to eradicate illiteracy from the tribal belts.
options: to eradicate illiteracy from the tribal belts.

questions.question: Had the locomotive driver applied (A) / the emergency air brakes on time, (B) / the catastrophic collision could be avoided. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the emergency air brakes on time,
the catastrophic collision could be avoided.
questions.explanation: This is an inverted Third Conditional construction (Had the driver applied is equivalent to If the driver had applied). The tracking main clause must contain $could / would + have + been + V_3$ to register past passive capability. Change "could be avoided" to "could have been avoided".

questions.question: I am working on this research manuscript (A) / since last Monday and I hope to finish (B) / the final draft by tomorrow evening. (C) / No Error (D)
options: I am working on this research manuscript
since last Monday and I hope to finish
the final draft by tomorrow evening.
questions.explanation: The point-in-time marker "since last Monday" forces the verb configuration out of the simple present continuous. Change "I am working" to "I have been working".

questions.question: The senior investigative journalist asked the minister (A) / that why he had refused to sign the global (B) / carbon emission reduction treaty. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The senior investigative journalist asked the minister
that why he had refused to sign the global
questions.explanation: Indirect Speech Interrogative Rule: When converting a Wh-question (why, what, where, how) into indirect narrative style, you must never use the conjunction "that" before the interrogative word. The Wh-word itself functions as the connector. Remove "that".

questions.question: The high-yield cash crop fields (A) / were completely ruined by the locust swarm (B) / before the local farmers can harvest them. (C) / No Error (D)
options: were completely ruined by the locust swarm
before the local farmers can harvest them.
questions.explanation: The sentence sets up its action baseline in the past passive voice ("were completely ruined"). Therefore, the capability auxiliary in the following clause must match this past perspective. Change "can harvest" to "could harvest".

questions.question: The judge requested the defense lawyer (A) / to call his next witness (B) / to the stand immediately. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The judge requested the defense lawyer
questions.explanation: This is a contextual reporting verb infraction in direct/indirect grammar. A judge does not "request" or plead with a lawyer in an official capacity within a court setting; a judge orders, directs, or instructs. Change "requested" to "ordered" or "directed".

questions.question: The multi-million dollar corporate fraud case (A) / is currently being investigating (B) / by a special task force of economic offenses wing. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The multi-million dollar corporate fraud case
by a special task force of economic offenses wing.
questions.explanation: In the Present Continuous Passive Voice framework, the structure must strictly adhere to: $is/am/are + being + V_3$ (Past Participle). The sentence mistakenly uses a present participle ($V_4$). Change "investigating" to "investigated".

questions.question: The medical board recommended that (A) / the injured athlete undergoes a comprehensive (B) / magnetic resonance imaging scan tomorrow morning. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the injured athlete undergoes a comprehensive
magnetic resonance imaging scan tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: Present Subjunctive Mood Rule: When a sentence contains a verb expressing a demand, recommendation, requirement, or mandate (recommend, suggest, insist, demand, require) followed by a "that" clause, the verb in the "that" clause must be in its base form ($V_1$), completely free of any singular 's' or 'es' endings, regardless of the subject. Change "undergoes" to "undergo".

questions.question: The prime minister enquired the officer (A) / if any civilian casualties had been reported (B) / during the border shelling incidents. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The prime minister enquired the officer
if any civilian casualties had been reported
questions.explanation: The verb "enquire" is an intransitive verb when followed by a personal object, meaning it requires the preposition "of" to connect to the entity being questioned. Change "enquired the officer" to "enquired of the officer" (or change the verb entirely to the transitive "asked the officer").

questions.question: The dynamic entrepreneur requested the investors (A) / that they should consider his innovative (B) / green energy business proposal favorably. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The dynamic entrepreneur requested the investors
that they should consider his innovative
questions.explanation: When formatting an imperative sentence or request into indirect speech, use a to-infinitive structure ($to + V_1$) to link the command/request, rather than a heavy "that" clause with modal verbs. Change "that they should consider" to "to consider".

questions.question: The ancient city ruins (A) / were excavated by the archaeology team (B) / a few decades ago. (C) / No Error (D)
options: were excavated by the archaeology team
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The past passive structure ($were + V_3$) aligns properly with the past time frame anchor "a few decades ago."

questions.question: The internal security directives require (A) / that every employee changes his access (B) / password credentials at the end of the month. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that every employee changes his access
password credentials at the end of the month.
questions.explanation: This is another Present Subjunctive Mood trap triggered by the mandate verb "require". The verb in the tracking clause must remain in its pure base form ($V_1$), completely ignoring the singular subject "every employee". Change "changes" to "change".

questions.question: The HR executive asked me (A) / what was my total work experience (B) / in the field of automated cloud architecture. (C) / No Error (D)
options: what was my total work experience
in the field of automated cloud architecture.
questions.explanation: Indirect Question Word Order: When an interrogative sentence is transformed into an indirect statement, it loses its questioning syntax. The sentence structure must switch from an inverted question form (verb + subject) back to an assertive statement form (subject + verb). Change "what was my total work experience" to "what my total work experience was".

questions.question: The corporate presentation slides (A) / have been prepared by the creative cell (B) / well in advance of the deadline. (C) / No Error (D)
options: have been prepared by the creative cell
well in advance of the deadline.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The Present Perfect Passive construction ($have + been + V_3$) is applied flawlessly.

questions.question: The command center ordered the fighter jet squad (A) / that they should immediately intercept (B) / the unidentified supersonic aerial vector. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The command center ordered the fighter jet squad
questions.explanation: Similar to Q232, an indirect imperative command structured with "ordered" should bypass a clunky "that... should" clause in favor of a clean to-infinitive structure. Change "that they should immediately intercept" to "to immediately intercept".

questions.question: It is absolutely imperative (A) / that the laboratory assistant handles (B) / the volatile organic chemical compounds with extreme care. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the volatile organic chemical compounds with extreme care.
questions.explanation: The adjective "imperative" belongs to the category of urgency markers (crucial, essential, vital, imperative, necessary) that trigger the Present Subjunctive Mood in an ensuing "that" clause. The verb must use its base form. Change "handles" to "handle".

questions.question: The suspect denied that (A) / he had not stolen the corporate layout designs (B) / from the research database vault. (C) / No Error (D)
options: he had not stolen the corporate layout designs
questions.explanation: The verb "deny" is inherently negative (meaning to state that something did not happen). Adding a secondary negative word like "not" inside the reported clause creates a double negative that reverses the intended meaning. Remove "not".

questions.question: The strategic border outposts (A) / are being continuously monitored (B) / by unmanned aerial reconnaissance drones. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The Present Continuous Passive voice sequence ($are + being + V_3$) is used correctly.

questions.question: The defense council insisted that (A) / the accused is released on bail (B) / pending the arrival of the forensic verification logs. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the accused is released on bail
pending the arrival of the forensic verification logs.
questions.explanation: The verb "insist" signals a strong demand, triggering the Present Subjunctive Mood. In the subjunctive mood, the standard present forms of the verb to be (is, am, are) are completely replaced by the base word "be". Change "is released" to "be released".

questions.question: The tax consultant enquired from me (A) / if I had filed my income returns (B) / within the officially stipulated timeframe windows. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The tax consultant enquired from me
if I had filed my income returns
within the officially stipulated timeframe windows.
questions.explanation: The idiomatically correct construction after "enquired" is to use the preposition "of", never "from". Change "enquired from me" to "enquired of me".

questions.question: The old woman prayed that (A) / God might showered his choicest blessings (B) / on the young couple's newborn infant. (C) / No Error (D)
options: God might showered his choicest blessings
on the young couple's newborn infant.
questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary verbs (might, may, should, could, would) must always be followed by the pure base form of the verb ($V_1$), never a past-tense or past-participle form ($V_3$). Change "showered" to "shower".

questions.question: The newly drafted standard operating procedures (A) / must be strictly follow by all the technical staff (B) / inside the semiconductor processing cleanrooms. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The newly drafted standard operating procedures
must be strictly follow by all the technical staff
questions.explanation: The passive voice structure for a modal verb is modal + be + V_3 (Past Participle). The sentence leaves the verb in its base form. Change "must be strictly follow" to "must be strictly followed".

questions.question: The principal demanded that (A) / the unruly student apologizes to the entire (B) / assembly before entering the classroom corridors. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the unruly student apologizes to the entire
assembly before entering the classroom corridors.
questions.explanation: The verb "demand" triggers the Present Subjunctive Mood. Drop the singular 's' from the verb to restore its base form. Change "apologizes" to "apologize".

questions.question: The senior architect asked the client (A) / that how long it would take to finalize (B) / the structural blueprints for the commercial complex. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The senior architect asked the client
that how long it would take to finalize
the structural blueprints for the commercial complex.
questions.explanation: As established in Q226, do not insert the conjunction "that" before an interrogative Wh-word (how long) when using indirect narrative style. Remove "that".

questions.question: The corporate embezzlement plans (A) / were exposed by a whistle-blower (B) / working inside the primary accounting branch. (C) / No Error (D)
options: working inside the primary accounting branch.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The past passive framework (were + V_3) matches the context perfectly.

questions.question: It is crucial that (A) / the flight navigation computer performs (B) / a complete systems diagnostic check before takeoff. (C) / No Error (D)
options: a complete systems diagnostic check before takeoff.
questions.explanation: The phrase "It is crucial that" mandates the use of the Present Subjunctive Mood. The verb must strip its singular ending to match the base form. Change "performs" to "perform".

questions.question: The factory supervisor told the labor force (A) / that they had better worked systematically (B) / to meet the steep festive export delivery targets. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The factory supervisor told the labor force
that they had better worked systematically
to meet the steep festive export delivery targets.
questions.explanation: The idiomatic phrase "had better" functions as a modal operator meaning should. It must be followed directly by a bare infinitive verb / base form (V_1), never a past-tense form (V_2/V_3). Change "had better worked" to "had better work".

questions.question: The global digital tender notices (A) / have been published in all leading business (B) / newspapers by the corporate communications cell. (C) / No Error (D)
options: have been published in all leading business
newspapers by the corporate communications cell.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. The present perfect passive construction (have + been + V_3) is used flawlessly.

questions.question: The quality of these newly imported (A) / semiconductor microchips from Taiwan are (B) / not up to the specified defense industrial standards. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The quality of these newly imported
not up to the specified defense industrial standards.
questions.explanation: Prepositional Phrase Interruption Trap: The true subject of the sentence is the singular noun "quality", not the plural object of the preposition "microchips". Therefore, the verb must be singular. Change "are" to "is".

questions.question: Neither the financial advisor nor (A) / the board directors has approved (B) / the aggressive capital expenditure budget. (C) / No Error (D)
questions.explanation: Proximity Rule: When subjects are joined by neither... nor or either... or, the verb must agree with its nearest subject. The nearest subject is "directors," which is plural. Change "has approved" to "have approved".

questions.question: The political leader, along with (A) / his core administrative team members, are (B) / expected to arrive at the media briefing room shortly. (C) / No Error (D)
options: his core administrative team members, are
expected to arrive at the media briefing room shortly.
questions.explanation: When a singular subject ("leader") is joined with other nouns using words like along with, together with, as well as, accompanied by, or besides, these phrases act as parenthetical insertions. They do not change the number of the subject. Change "are" to "is".

questions.question: A large number of automated (A) / assembly line robots has been deployed (B) / to accelerate the smartphone production cycle. (C) / No Error (D)
options: assembly line robots has been deployed
to accelerate the smartphone production cycle.
questions.explanation: "A large number of" + Plural Noun takes a plural verb (indicates an indefinite large quantity). "The number of" + Plural Noun takes a singular verb (indicates a specific numeric count). Change "has been deployed" to "have been deployed".

questions.question: Three-fourths of the core corporate (A) / infrastructure budget have already been allocated (B) / to the cyber security upgrade project. (C) / No Error (D)
options: infrastructure budget have already been allocated
to the cyber security upgrade project.
questions.explanation: When fractions or percentages are used, the verb agrees with the noun following the "of" modifier. Since "infrastructure budget" is an uncountable/singular noun, the fraction remains singular. Change "have already been" to "has already been".

questions.question: The behavior of the violent protestors (A) / were highly unpredictable, causing a massive panic (B) / among the local shop owners down the street. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The behavior of the violent protestors
were highly unpredictable, causing a massive panic
among the local shop owners down the street.
questions.explanation: The true subject is the singular noun "behavior". The plural noun "protestors" is merely the object of the preposition. Change "were" to "was".

questions.question: Many a dynamic young scholar (A) / fail to secure a research fellowship (B) / due to poorly framed project synopsis presentations. (C) / No Error (D)
options: fail to secure a research fellowship
due to poorly framed project synopsis presentations.
questions.explanation: The idiomatic phrase "Many a" is strictly followed by a singular noun and a singular verb. While "young scholar" is correctly singular, the verb must match. Change "fail" to "fails".

questions.question: Two thousand dollars are (A) / a highly reasonable price to pay (B) / for this customized high-end industrial server workstation. (C) / No Error (D)
options: a highly reasonable price to pay
for this customized high-end industrial server workstation.
questions.explanation: When a specific sum of money, distance, time, or weight is stated as a single lump sum or collective quantity, it takes a singular verb. Change "are" to "is".

questions.question: Gulliver's Travels, a famous satirical masterpiece, (A) / were written by Jonathan Swift (B) / during the early eighteenth century era. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Gulliver's Travels, a famous satirical masterpiece,
during the early eighteenth century era.
questions.explanation: Titles of books, plays, movies, or musical works are always treated as singular entities, even if the title itself contains a plural noun (Travels). Change "were written" to "was written".

questions.question: Not only the managing partners (A) / but also the principal structural engineer (B) / were held liable for the building collapse. (C) / No Error (D)
options: but also the principal structural engineer
were held liable for the building collapse.
questions.explanation: For not only... but also constructions, apply the proximity rule. The nearest subject to the verb is "the principal structural engineer," which is singular. Change "were" to "was".

questions.question: Every window, every door, and every ventilation (A) / duct were meticulously inspected by the forensic (B) / investigation crew before sealing the house premises. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Every window, every door, and every ventilation
duct were meticulously inspected by the forensic
investigation crew before sealing the house premises.
questions.explanation: When multiple singular nouns are connected by "and" but are preceded by "each" or "every", the overall compound subject remains strictly singular. Change "were meticulously" to "was meticulously".

questions.question: The jury was completely divided (A) / in their opinions regarding the ultimate sentence (B) / to be handed down to the corporate criminal. (C) / No Error (D)
options: in their opinions regarding the ultimate sentence
to be handed down to the corporate criminal.
questions.explanation: This is the reverse of Q101. The plural possessive tracking pronoun "their opinions" tells you that the collective noun "jury" is acting as split individuals. Therefore, the verb must match this plural division. Change "was completely divided" to "were completely divided".

questions.question: More than one engineering student (A) / have cleared the initial technical round (B) / of the campus placement drive today. (C) / No Error (D)
options: have cleared the initial technical round
of the campus placement drive today.
questions.explanation: The phrase "More than one" takes a singular noun and a singular verb. Change "have cleared" to "has cleared". (Note: "More than two" takes plural, and "More students than one" takes plural).

questions.question: The performance metrics data (A) / collected from the manufacturing plants (B) / is highly encouraging for the investment board. (C) / No Error (D)
options: is highly encouraging for the investment board.
questions.explanation: In traditional grammar, "data" is the plural form of "datum" and requires a plural verb. While modern English sometimes accepts data as collective singular, TCS strictly enforces traditional plural usage for "data" and "criteria". Change "is" to "are".

questions.question: Either your security credentials (A) / or your automated access token card (B) / need to be updated before the system migration lock. (C) / No Error (D)
options: or your automated access token card
need to be updated before the system migration lock.
questions.explanation: By the proximity rule for either... or, the verb must agree with "your automated access token card," which is a singular subject. Change "need" to "needs".

questions.question: Rice and dal are (A) / the staple comforting food item (B) / for a vast majority of households in East India. (C) / No Error (D)
options: for a vast majority of households in East India.
questions.explanation: When two nouns express a single, unified concept, collective dish, or item (Rice and dal, Bread and butter, Time and tide), they take a singular verb. This is reinforced by the singular noun phrase "food item" later in the sentence. Change "are" to "is".

questions.question: The number of cyber security infractions (A) / tracking through our primary firewalls (B) / have dropped significantly over the past quarter. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The number of cyber security infractions
have dropped significantly over the past quarter.
questions.explanation: As mentioned in Q254, the specific phrase "The number of" targets a singular count entity. It must take a singular verb. Change "have dropped" to "has dropped".

questions.question: Ten kilometers are a very long distance (A) / to cover on foot for an untrained (B) / civilian volunteer during hot summers. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Ten kilometers are a very long distance
to cover on foot for an untrained
questions.explanation: A specific unit of distance ("Ten kilometers") viewed as a singular, unified measurement takes a singular verb. Change "are" to "is".

questions.question: One of the most common mistakes (A) / made by amateur traders are over-leveraging (B) / their accounts during high-volatility market sessions. (C) / No Error (D)
options: One of the most common mistakes
made by amateur traders are over-leveraging
their accounts during high-volatility market sessions.
questions.explanation: In the "One of + Plural Noun" structure, the true subject is the singular pronoun "One". The verb must always be singular. Change "are over-leveraging" to "is over-leveraging".

questions.question: The keys of the secondary automated (A) / locker system was mistakenly left (B) / on the security desk floor last night. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The keys of the secondary automated
on the security desk floor last night.
questions.explanation: The true subject is the plural noun "keys". Do not let the intervening prepositional phrase "of the locker system" fool you into using a singular verb. Change "was mistakenly left" to "were mistakenly left".

questions.question: Athletics are playing a very crucial role (A) / in fostering physical resilience and a spirit (B) / of competitive sportsmanship among school students. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Athletics are playing a very crucial role
in fostering physical resilience and a spirit
of competitive sportsmanship among school students.
questions.explanation: Names of sciences, academic subjects, or physical activities ending in '-ics' (Athletics, Physics, Mathematics, Economics, Politics) are singular in form and use a singular verb when speaking about the general discipline. Change "are playing" to "is playing".

questions.question: Neither of the technical solutions (A) / proposed by the external consultants (B) / were found viable by the board. (C) / No Error (D)
options: were found viable by the board.
questions.explanation: The distributive pronoun "Neither" means "none of the two" and acts as an exclusive singular subject. It must be paired with a singular verb. Change "were found" to "was found".

questions.question: Nothing but cold water streams (A) / was visible to the stranded hikers (B) / down the massive mountain gorge landscape. (C) / No Error (D)
options: was visible to the stranded hikers
down the massive mountain gorge landscape.
questions.explanation: The sentence is No Error. When a sentence begins with "Nothing but", the verb is always singular, regardless of whether the noun following "but" is singular or plural. "Was" is correct.

questions.question: The crew members was safely rescued (A) / from the capsized merchant cargo vessel (B) / by the Indian Coast Guard helicopter team. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The crew members was safely rescued
from the capsized merchant cargo vessel
by the Indian Coast Guard helicopter team.
questions.explanation: The sentence explicitly specifies the plural subject "crew members" (the individual individuals), which requires a plural verb. Change "was safely rescued" to "were safely rescued".

questions.question: Here come the senior chief operating (A) / officer along with his executive advisors (B) / to audit our performance metrics logs. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Here come the senior chief operating
officer along with his executive advisors
to audit our performance metrics logs.
questions.explanation: In sentences starting with here or there, the true subject sits after the verb. The subject is "the senior chief operating officer," which is singular. (The phrase "along with..." does not pluralize the subject). Change "Here come" to "Here comes".

questions.question: The dynamic marketing executive likes (A) / analyzing consumer patterns, creating ad campaigns, (B) / and to negotiate deals with potential clients. (C) / No Error (D)
options: analyzing consumer patterns, creating ad campaigns,
and to negotiate deals with potential clients.
questions.explanation: Parallel Structure Violation: Elements in a series linked by coordinating conjunctions must match in form. The first two items use the gerund form (analyzing, creating), so the third item must match. Change "to negotiate deals" to "negotiating deals".

questions.question: The international diplomatic mission (A) / returned back to their home country (B) / after the peace talk rounds collapsed. (C) / No Error (D)
options: returned back to their home country
after the peace talk rounds collapsed.
questions.explanation: Redundancy Trap: The word "return" itself means to go or come back. Adding the word "back" right after it introduces a textbook redundancy infraction. Remove "back".

questions.question: The operations analyst is responsible for (A) / updating database fields, sorting invoice files, (B) / and the verification of user identity tracking logs. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The operations analyst is responsible for
updating database fields, sorting invoice files,
and the verification of user identity tracking logs.
questions.explanation: To maintain strict structural parallelism with the preceding gerund phrase elements (updating fields, sorting files), the final element must use the same syntax. Change "the verification of user identity tracking logs" to "verifying user identity tracking logs".

questions.question: I requested the senior flight attendant (A) / to kindly repeat the safety evacuation (B) / announcement once again. (C) / No Error (D)
options: I requested the senior flight attendant
to kindly repeat the safety evacuation
questions.explanation: Redundancy Trap: The verb "repeat" means to state or do something again. Combining it with the phrase "once again" is completely redundant. Remove "once again".

questions.question: The corporate legal policy is (A) / not only comprehensive in its scope (B) / but it is also highly flexible in its execution. (C) / No Error (D)
options: not only comprehensive in its scope
but it is also highly flexible in its execution.
questions.explanation: To keep things balanced on both sides of the not only... but also frame, the grammatical structure should match closely: Not only + Adjective phrase ("comprehensive in its scope"); But also should link directly to an adjective phrase, without inserting a clunky new subject-verb combo ("but it is also"). Change part C to: "but also highly flexible in its execution".

questions.question: In my opinion, I think (A) / the newly proposed real estate project (B) / will struggle to attract premium home buyers. (C) / No Error (D)
options: the newly proposed real estate project
will struggle to attract premium home buyers.
questions.explanation: "In my opinion" and "I think" express the exact same concept. Using both in the same clause is redundant. Change to either "In my opinion," or "I think".

questions.question: The senior software engineer's tasks (A) / include debugging legacy codes, writing technical documentation, (B) / and to train the junior engineering recruits. (C) / No Error (D)
options: include debugging legacy codes, writing technical documentation,
and to train the junior engineering recruits.
questions.explanation: The list uses gerund forms (debugging, writing). Change the infinitive "to train" to the parallel gerund form "training".

questions.question: The multi-national enterprise (A) / will advance forward with its expansion (B) / plans despite the global financial slump. (C) / No Error (D)
options: will advance forward with its expansion
plans despite the global financial slump.
questions.explanation: Redundancy Trap: "Advance" means to move forward. Adding the word "forward" is unnecessary. Remove "forward".

questions.question: The primary suspect was accused of (A) / forging administrative signatures, embezzling corporate funds, (B) / and he committed tax evasion over several years. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The primary suspect was accused of
forging administrative signatures, embezzling corporate funds,
and he committed tax evasion over several years.
questions.explanation: To preserve parallel structure across the series of offenses modifying "accused of," change the full clause "and he committed tax evasion" into a matching gerund phrase: "and committing tax evasion".

questions.question: The technical committee members (A) / unanimously agreed together on the final choice (B) / of the software vendor platform. (C) / No Error (D)
